question_papers.paper_title: Set 1 - How do Organisms Reproduce? Practice Paper

questions.question_text: Which of the following organisms reproduces naturally through regeneration?
options: Amoeba
Planaria
Rhizopus
Spirogyra
questions.correct_answer: Planaria

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements correctly describes key observations in How do Organisms Reproduce? (Set 1)?
options: Core process in How do Organisms Reproduce? obeys conservation laws and standard reaction conditions.
Process in How do Organisms Reproduce? violates mass conservation.
No physical or chemical state change occurs during the reaction.
Products have higher total mass than initial reactants.
questions.correct_answer: Core process in How do Organisms Reproduce? obeys conservation laws and standard reaction conditions.

questions.question_text: What physical state symbol or indicator color change is associated with How do Organisms Reproduce? (Set 1)?
options: Aqueous solution (aq) with characteristic color change
Solid precipitate (s) with gas emission
Gaseous phase (g) only
Liquid phase (l) with zero temperature change
questions.correct_answer: Aqueous solution (aq) with characteristic color change

questions.question_text: Identify the correct SI unit or mathematical relationship relevant to How do Organisms Reproduce? (Set 1).
options: Standard NCERT Formula & Unit
Dimensionless Ratio x 100
Inverse Square Exponential
Absolute Constant Zero

questions.question_text:

Reason (R): Molecular and atomic rearrangements preserve total mass, charge, and energy balance.

Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.correct_answer: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A

question_papers.paper_title: Set 4 - How do Organisms Reproduce? Practice Paper

questions.question_text: What is vegetative propagation? State two agricultural advantages of using this method.
options: Option A
Option B
Option C
Option D
questions.correct_answer: Vegetative propagation is an asexual mode where new plants grow from vegetative parts (root, stem, leaf). Advantages: 1. Plants bear flowers and fruits much faster. 2. Preserves exact desirable genetic characteristics of parent plants.

question_papers.paper_title: Set 5 - How do Organisms Reproduce? Practice Paper

questions.question_text: Describe the structure and functions of the Placenta during human pregnancy.
options: Option A
Option B
Option C
Option D
questions.correct_answer: Placenta is a disc-like tissue embedded in the uterine wall containing embryonic villi surrounded by maternal blood spaces. Functions: Supplies oxygen and glucose to the fetus and removes metabolic wastes (urea, CO2) into mother's blood.
